findings.summary: The public experience does not respond to the user’s dark color-scheme preference.
findings.evidence: The dark-mode screenshot remains a white surface, matching the light capture; the computed root color-scheme is "normal".
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme and provide preference-driven surface and text tokens with prefers-color-scheme or light-dark().

findings.summary: Route and major state changes do not use View Transitions.
findings.evidence: The live feature probe found no view-transition usage across the guest homepage, while navigation and modal state changes are prominent.
findings.suggestedFix: Use same-document or cross-document View Transitions for route and substantial state changes, with reduced-motion handling.

findings.summary: The long guest homepage offers no scroll-state-aware navigation or progress affordance.
findings.evidence: Mobile layout measured a 7,330px document, while the screenshot and DOM show static navigation and the probe found no scroll-timeline usage.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a restrained scrollability/progress cue or scroll-state-aware header where it helps users orient on the long page.

findings.summary: Jobs search is interrupted on load by an authentication modal that obscures the primary results journey.
findings.evidence: The desktop jobs capture shows a modal and dimmed results before user interaction; the DOM reports five role=dialog sections, including four empty duplicates.
findings.suggestedFix: Let guests inspect the initial result/detail state before prompting, and implement one semantic dialog with a clear accessible name and predictable light dismiss.

findings.summary: The jobs authentication overlay is built from duplicated custom role=dialog sections rather than one robust dialog primitive.
findings.evidence: The jobs probe found five SECTION[role=dialog][aria-modal=true] nodes, four empty and the visible one without an accessible label.
findings.suggestedFix: Consolidate the overlay into one native dialog, label it, and use platform focus management and dismissal behavior.

findings.summary: Top Content omits the viewport meta tag and is rendered as a 980px desktop canvas scaled down on a 360px device.
findings.evidence: The mobile layout reports clientWidth 980, scale 0.367 and hasViewportMeta false; the DOM and content probe independently confirm no viewport meta.
findings.suggestedFix: Add width=device-width, initial-scale=1 and ensure cards/navigation reflow at the actual narrow viewport.

findings.summary: The guest jobs journey cannot proceed without immediately dismissing or satisfying an authentication gate.
findings.evidence: Jobs results load behind an automatic sign-in modal; this blocks inspection of the selected result and interrupts the primary guest task.
findings.suggestedFix: Defer the authentication gate until an action truly requires membership and preserve the user’s search/result context through sign-in.

findings.summary: Empty sign-in and signup submissions provide no visible error or recovery guidance in the exercised state.
findings.evidence: Before and after empty-submit screenshots are visually identical and the forms expose non-required fields to the DOM; no inline error or summary appears.
findings.suggestedFix: Validate after interaction, mark invalid fields, announce errors, and move focus to a concise recovery summary without clearing user input.

findings.summary: Largest Contentful Paint is slower than the good threshold on the audited guest homepage.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured LCP at 3.5s (score 0.64), while the unthrottled trace measured 1.42s, indicating the constrained-load path is the risk.
findings.suggestedFix: Prioritize the LCP resource and remove discovery/render-blocking delays; verify on representative mobile conditions.

findings.summary: The guest homepage ships a script-heavy critical path with a parser stylesheet and avoidable transfer cost.
findings.evidence: HAR recorded 605KB transferred, including 505KB script; the stylesheet is a VeryHigh-priority parser candidate, and Lighthouse flags LCP discovery/network dependency issues.
findings.suggestedFix: Reduce critical CSS/JS, confirm non-critical scripts are deferred, and explicitly prioritize the true LCP asset.

findings.summary: A large share of downloaded JavaScript and CSS is unused on the guest homepage.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse estimates 309KiB unused JavaScript and 44KiB unused CSS, including several bundles with roughly 48% to 77% waste.
findings.suggestedFix: Split guest-only entry bundles, conditionally load authentication/analytics dependencies, and remove unused CSS from the initial route.

findings.summary: The jobs modal accessibility tree contains duplicated unnamed dialog roles.
findings.evidence: The DOM probe reports five aria-modal dialogs, four empty and the visible dialog without aria-label; this can produce confusing screen-reader navigation despite the homepage Lighthouse score of 0.97.
findings.suggestedFix: Expose exactly one named dialog and remove hidden duplicates from the accessibility tree.

findings.summary: The homepage logs a failed tracking-pixel network error.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse errors-in-console reports net::ERR_NAME_NOT_RESOLVED for ponf.linkedin.com/pixel/tracking.png.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove or repair the failing tracking endpoint and ensure optional telemetry failures stay silent and non-disruptive.

findings.summary: Image markup does not reserve dimensions, and the mobile hero is rendered at the wrong aspect ratio.
findings.evidence: The image primitive found 7/7 images without width/height and 7/7 without srcset; Lighthouse identifies the hero displayed at 1.75 versus an intrinsic 1.25 ratio.
findings.suggestedFix: Provide intrinsic width/height or aspect-ratio, preserve object proportions, and add responsive image candidates.

findings.summary: The page misses browser-platform diagnostics and back/forward cache opportunities.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reports a missing source map for a large first-party bundle and three bfcache failure reasons tied to Cache-Control: no-store.
findings.suggestedFix: Publish production source maps to authorized tooling and scope no-store only to responses that genuinely contain sensitive per-user data.

findings.summary: Public jobs/content pages expose rich entities without structured data.
findings.evidence: Live probes found zero JSON-LD blocks on the homepage, jobs search, and Top Content, although titles, descriptions, canonical links, hreflang, and Open Graph metadata are present.
findings.suggestedFix: Add content-matched schema.org JSON-LD for relevant public entities such as JobPosting, ItemList, Organization, and article/content objects.
findings.guidanceId: structured data schema.org json-ld open graph social preview metadata

findings.summary: Security policy coverage is incomplete despite strong HTTPS, HSTS, CSP, framing, and MIME protections.
findings.evidence: Headers show HTTPS, HSTS, CSP, nosniff and sameorigin framing, but no Referrer-Policy or Permissions-Policy; the CSP requires unsafe-inline for styles and all eight cookies use SameSite=None.
findings.suggestedFix: Set explicit Referrer-Policy and Permissions-Policy, tighten inline style policy where feasible, and use the least-permissive SameSite mode per cookie.

findings.summary: Guest sign-in and signup default to keeping the user signed in.
findings.evidence: Both captured account forms show a preselected “Keep me signed in” or “Remember me” checkbox, extending session persistence unless the user notices and opts out.
findings.suggestedFix: Default persistent sign-in off, or clearly explain duration and device risk before the user opts in.
findings.guidanceId: honest defaults no dark patterns confirmshaming forced continuity consent

findings.summary: Asset delivery misses responsive-image and dimension optimizations.
findings.evidence: The image audit found no srcset or explicit dimensions on all seven inspected images; Lighthouse confirms an aspect-ratio distortion.
findings.suggestedFix: Serve correctly sized responsive candidates and reserve stable image boxes before bytes arrive.

findings.summary: Most guest-page transfer is attributed to secondary LinkedIn origins and scripts.
findings.evidence: HAR recorded 576,476 of 604,965 transferred bytes across non-www origins, with 505KB of script and 28 of 41 requests classified as third-party by origin.
findings.suggestedFix: Set a guest-route script/third-party byte budget and conditionally load telemetry and identity dependencies only when needed.

findings.summary: High-value public job and content capabilities are not exposed as structured agent tools.
findings.evidence: The live homepage probe found no model-context/WebMCP registration, while the site exposes agent-suitable search, content exploration, login, and signup workflows.
findings.suggestedFix: Expose narrowly scoped, user-confirmed WebMCP tools for public search and navigation while keeping sensitive account actions gated.
